identity.title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation

problem.claim: How LLM performance changes when users develop or refine underspecified needs through multi-turn conversation.

gap.claim: Despite frequent underspecification in real instructions, evaluation has mainly studied single-turn, fully specified prompts.

contributions.claim: A large-scale simulation comparison of LLM performance in single- versus multi-turn settings.
A decomposition of multi-turn degradation into a minor aptitude loss and a significant increase in unreliability.
An account in which early assumptions and premature solution attempts create errors that models overly rely on and fail to recover from.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present the multi-turn performance comparison and degradation decomposition as discoveries of this work.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The tested open- and closed-weight LLMs reportedly perform significantly worse in multi-turn conversations, with an average 39% drop across six generation tasks.
Analysis of more than 200,000 simulated conversations reportedly attributes degradation mainly to increased unreliability rather than loss of aptitude.
The authors report that models often make early assumptions, attempt final answers prematurely, and do not recover after a wrong turn.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs could help users define and refine needs through conversation, not only execute fully specified tasks.
Conversation logs show underspecification is frequent, while evaluation has emphasized single-turn fully specified instructions.
The work compares LLM performance across single- and multi-turn settings using large-scale simulations.
Across six tasks, the authors report a 39% average multi-turn drop, linked chiefly to unreliability, early assumptions, premature answers, and failed recovery.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs an aggregate performance gap with a decomposition into aptitude loss and unreliability, then gives a conversational failure pattern explaining the latter.

lessons.interpretation: This alignment makes a broad benchmark result more diagnostically useful.
lessons.application: When reporting interactive-system degradation, pair the headline metric with a component breakdown and an observable failure sequence.
lessons.exception: This is less suitable when the study cannot measure or distinguish the proposed components.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the tested models, six tasks, metrics, significance procedure, or simulation protocol.
It does not specify how aptitude and unreliability were operationalized or how realistic the simulated conversations were.
The abstract does not report recovery rates, error distributions, or comparisons among individual models.
